trigger: an operator reads audit-log.md's or server-admin.md's pre-existing unconditional claim that a service-scoped API token 'can still disable ... a runaway schedule' as a kill-switch fallback during an incident
summary: The claim was accurate when written but is falsified by #3378, a kill-switch-reachability gap this same branch's investigation discovered while verifying deny_service_scoped_schedule was provably dead (Schedule:Write is checked unconditionally before `enabled` is parsed, so a service-scoped token is denied on disable too, not just enable/create). Fixed in commit b8aa77dcd by adding a caveat pointing to #3378 in both docs; the underlying #3378 gap itself is deliberately NOT fixed in this branch (see BR1A-13).

trigger: a future engineer reads this branch's own retirement comment in workflow_routes.cpp and believes GET /fragments/schedules has no permission gate to run after the deny
summary: First-draft comment (commit 4e2856d9e) incorrectly claimed the fragment 'has no permission gate of its own to run after' when retiring the now-provably-dead deny_service_scoped_schedule_list caller nearby — false, perm_fn(Schedule,Read) runs immediately below. A comment contradicting the code is a truth finding per the docs-writer/domain-agent split; security-guardian caught it since the claim was about a permission gate. Fixed in b8aa77dcd, correctly reclassifying this site as live-but-redundant (bucket 1b), not gate-less.

trigger: compiling schedule_routes.cpp after deny_service_scoped_schedule's definition (its only caller of spdlog) was deleted
summary: Dead #include <spdlog/spdlog.h> left behind after removing the only call site that used it (the retired function's audit-log try/catch). Independently found by both cpp-expert and cpp-safety in the same Gate 3 pass. Fixed in commit 9ef49c967.

trigger: an auditor or incident responder searches audit-log.md's schedule.create/.enable/.disable/.delete rows for the audit verb a denied service-scoped call actually emits
summary: The four schedule rows still described the route's own now-dead interim deny as the emitting mechanism, when require_permission's default-deny (auth.permission_required, empty target) has actually been the real emitting path since guardian-confinement-2298 PR 3 ('the flip'), well before this branch. Reworded across the Gate 3/Gate 6 fix cycle to state the audit verb accurately; final wording landed in 5a9444cac.

trigger: GET /api/schedules (list), DELETE /api/schedules/{id}, and POST /api/schedules/{id}/enable have zero route-level tests; only POST /api/schedules (create) has one
summary: This is exactly the coverage shape that let #3378 (the enable-route kill-switch gap) go undetected. Bounded blast radius (missing coverage, not a false-green), so SHOULD not a policy floor per the governance rules; does not block this PR. Filed as issue #3390 (governance-deferred label) rather than added inline, to keep bucket 1a a zero-behavior-change retirement PR.

trigger: reading the retirement date recorded in the edited routed-concern row against the actual commit date
summary: Date typo (2026-08-20 instead of the actual 2026-08-21) in two places in the 'the flip' row's per-file-helper enumeration edit. Fixed in commit 1e20e1f80, alongside adding a cross-reference to #3390.

trigger: an operator reads server-admin.md's 'What to do' paragraph, which still said a service-scoped token 'can still disable ... a runaway schedule' as a fallback two paragraphs below this same PR's own #3378 caveat stating that guarantee does not currently hold
summary: Direct self-contradiction within the same file, introduced by this branch's own earlier (incomplete) fix for BR1A-1: the caveat was added but the fallback sentence a few paragraphs later wasn't updated to match. Independently found by both sre and enterprise-readiness in the same Gate 6 pass. Fixed in commit 5a9444cac to point at a non-service-scoped credential instead, with a pointer back to the caveat.

trigger: a SOC 2 auditor reads audit-log.md's schedule rows and infers the audit-verb behavior changed at this PR's 2026-08-21 merge, when it actually changed at 'the flip' (guardian-confinement-2298 PR 3), well before this branch existed
summary: The Gate 3/architect wording fix (BR1A-4) correctly described the current audit verb but still implied the behavior itself changed now rather than at the flip. Reworded in commit 5a9444cac to separate 'when the audit-verb behavior actually changed' from 'when the already-dead code was formally removed.' Also suggested filing an issue for a dedicated auth.permission_required row (no existing row despite it being the real enforcement/audit signal for every require_permission-gated route) - filed as #3391.

trigger: the next release assembles all pending changelog.d/ fragments verbatim into CHANGELOG.md, including changelog.d/3156-guardian-confinement.security.md (an unreleased fragment from an earlier, separate PR, #3156), which still asserted twice that a service-scoped token 'can still disable' or has 'disable remains reachable as the kill switch' for a runaway schedule
summary: Same underlying false claim as BR1A-1/BR1A-7, found one file further out during Gate 8's re-review of the fix diff, in a file this branch had not otherwise touched. Since #3156's fragment has not shipped in any released CHANGELOG.md yet, corrected in place to match the #3378 reality rather than let stale incident-response guidance ship (precedent for editing a pending fragment: 66797c5c6, #2442). Fixed in commit 1d5d1599c (both instances, lines 11 and 23).

trigger: reading the reworded schedule.enable/.disable and schedule.delete rows in audit-log.md ('This has audited as ...', an awkward perfect-tense construction) and server-admin.md ('or (see the #3378 caveat above) reliably disable', where 'reliably' implies intermittent success but the caveat states the deny is unconditional)
summary: Two cosmetic wording findings, both non-blocking (NICE, meaning is unambiguous in context). Applied anyway since both were cheap and 'reliably' specifically risked misleading an incident responder skimming only that sentence into retrying the token. Fixed in commit ec3fa18e5.

trigger: audit-log.md's schedule.list row (line 185, untouched by this branch) ties 'no longer emits this verb on denial' to bucket 1a retirement without separately noting the interim deny had already stopped mattering at the flip - the same shape BR1A-4/BR1A-8 fixed on the three rows above it
summary: Milder than the pre-fix versions of the rows above it (already softens the claim: 'already caught by the Schedule:Read gate first'). Non-blocking; recorded here so a future pass applies the same three-row treatment rather than this being silently dropped.

trigger: re-reading the Gate 6 fix commit for accuracy against code
summary: PASS overall; one trivial optional wording hedge noted, explicitly not required. Not applied - genuinely optional, distinct from BR1A-10/BR1A-11 which were applied despite also being NICE.

trigger: an operator holding only a service-scoped API token attempts to disable a runaway or compromised recurring schedule as their documented kill switch during an incident, on the current code (unchanged by this branch)
summary: Discovered while hand-verifying deny_service_scoped_schedule was provably dead code for retirement: require_permission's Schedule:Write check runs unconditionally before the enable route parses `enabled`, so a service-scoped token is denied on disable exactly as it is on enable/create - the documented 'disable always stays reachable' kill-switch guarantee does not hold, and never has, since guardian-confinement-2298 PR 3 landed. This predates this branch and this branch's own diff does not change the runtime behavior (a zero-behavior-change dead-code retirement). Per explicit user direction (AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-20: 'File an issue, continue bucket 1a only'), scoped OUT of this PR and filed as #3378 rather than fixed inline; every doc site this branch touches that referenced the old (false) guarantee was corrected to caveat it instead (BR1A-1, BR1A-7, BR1A-9). Recorded here at its derived band for transparency - deferral reflects an explicit scoping decision, not a swept-under-the-rug gap.
